title: Deterministic deployment removes overlap
diagnosis: The observation concerns unrestricted off-policy identification from deployment data alone.
correction: Causal learning can still use earlier randomized data, renewed exploration or additional structural assumptions.

title: Fixed versus learned policy
diagnosis: The unbiasedness calculation is for a fixed policy, not the maximized value on training data.
correction: Evaluate a fixed policy, or evaluate on data independent of policy learning.

title: The first IPW expectation drops the outcome
diagnosis: The scan omits Y_i in the first expectation.
correction: Insert Y_i; consistency then permits Y_i(pi(X_i)).

title: Minimax regret and pointwise rates
diagnosis: The red superefficiency remark mixes learning regret and fixed-policy value estimation.
correction: Faster regret at easier distributions can coexist with a worst-case n^-1/2 rate.

title: Conditions for uniform oracle equivalence
diagnosis: The norms, overlap, moment envelope and class growth are not specified.
correction: Use cross-fitting, L2 consistency, o(n^-1/2) nuisance error product, bounded estimated propensities and controlled complexity.

title: Interpret the efficient-score second moment
diagnosis: The author doubts the informal optimality statement.
correction: V*=E(Gamma*)^2; fixed-policy advantage variance is V*-A(pi)^2.

title: More covariates do not automatically remove confounding
diagnosis: Richer adjustment is a heuristic, not a monotone property of ignorability.
correction: Choose a valid adjustment set; even a pretreatment collider may introduce bias.

title: Sequential identification needs support
diagnosis: Sequential ignorability alone does not identify every policy.
correction: Require consistency, no interference and positive probability of target actions at reachable histories.

title: Feedback example: missing data and ambiguous indexing
diagnosis: The scan writes zero conditional means and omits the original outcome table; W is undefined.
correction: The corresponding uncentered lecture example gives 60; zero needs unstated centering. Specify treatment sequences.

title: Bellman analogy and the policy argument
diagnosis: The marginal Bellman equation suppresses policy/action averaging and assumes a Markov reward model.
correction: For a deterministic Markov policy use r(s,pi(s)) and P(sprime|s,pi(s)).

title: Transition factors need the next covariate
diagnosis: The source and official notes factor (W_t,X_{t+1}) with X_t transition terms.
correction: Replace X_t by X_{t+1} in both transition factors.

title: Condition the one-step probability on history
diagnosis: The source omits conditioning and flags it with a red question.
correction: Use P[W_1=pi_1(X_1)|F_1]. An unconditional denominator is valid only when this conditional matching probability is constant in the history; W_1 independent of X_1 alone is insufficient for a varying policy.

title: Initialize the IPW recursion at one
diagnosis: The source and official lecture write gamma_i0=0.
correction: Use gamma_i0=1, the empty product.

title: Backward evaluation versus optimization
diagnosis: The Q-learning label connects related ideas but the recursion evaluates a fixed policy.
correction: Optimal Q-learning adds maximization over actions.

title: Conditions for sequential double robustness
diagnosis: The handwritten unbiasedness claim lacks independence of nuisance fitting and the scope of correct models.
correction: With gamma0=1, true probabilities permit arbitrary fixed or independently trained value functions; true value functions permit positive predictable probability models.

title: Match the imposed intervention value
diagnosis: The condition X_j=w_j disagrees with do(X_j=x_j).
correction: Use X_j=x_j; divide out the old observational factor.

title: Continuous interventions require a point mass
diagnosis: The ratio is written as if every variable has a probability mass function.
correction: For continuous forced coordinates use a Dirac mass times the remaining conditional kernels.

title: Quantify over every path
diagnosis: The source starts with an arbitrary path but later refers to blocking one path.
correction: D-separation requires every path between the sets to be blocked.

title: Completeness is relative to a causal model
diagnosis: Failure of one attempted derivation is not nonidentifiability.
correction: No valid reduction may exist in the specified graph, model and observed-variable set.

title: Back-door special case mistranslated
diagnosis: The previous translation invented a root-node condition.
correction: Restored the condition: W and Y singleton, W has no descendants except Y.

title: Unspecified was reversed to specified
diagnosis: The red margin says all factors except w remain unspecified.
correction: Restored unspecified: the other random inputs are not fixed by do(W=w).

title: A counterfactual variable is not its distribution
diagnosis: The scan and official lecture equate a distribution to a structural random variable.
correction: Write Y(0,Z(1))=f_Y(0,f_Z(1,epsilon_Z),epsilon_Y); use its law for a distribution.

title: Potential outcomes can express nested counterfactuals
diagnosis: The notebook denies that potential-outcome notation can express this combination without a graph.
correction: Y(0,Z(1)) is standard potential-outcome notation; identification is separate.

title: Answer to the margin question: which identification assumptions?
diagnosis: The author asks whether the nested operation is identifiable.
correction: The fully observed independent-error SEM and sufficient support give a mediation formula; weaker models need not.

title: The UCB regret statement is an upper bound
diagnosis: The scan and official notes write equality although the proof only bounds arm counts.
correction: Use <= and sum only over positive gaps.

title: A uniform worst case cannot allow unbounded mean gaps
diagnosis: The red note claims a uniform bound while Gaussian means have no bounded range.
correction: Retain initial-pull sum Delta_k; a uniform K sqrt(T log T) scale needs bounded gaps.

title: Time-changed observations belong to arm k
diagnosis: The scan uses arm 0 in two lines while defining draws from arm k.
correction: Use Y_l prime(k); couple to an IID reward stream for each arm.

title: Resolve the unfinished Gaussian tail calculation
diagnosis: The author correctly doubts bounded Hoeffding for unbounded Gaussian rewards; per-count 1/T is too weak for union over T counts.
correction: Use a two-sided Gaussian T^-2 tail for each count, then union over KT pairs.

title: The count argument needs the other deviation direction
diagnosis: The one-sided event cannot upper bound the suboptimal arm sample mean.
correction: Use the simultaneous two-sided event; mu_star<=muhat_k+r_k<=mu_k+2r_k.

title: The UCB parenthesis was translated too specifically
diagnosis: The prior treatment-amount interpretation is not clearly supported by the difficult parenthesis.
correction: Use the arm-specific uncertainty context and retain uncertainty about the wording.

title: Best-arm ties and the Thompson heuristic
diagnosis: The probabilities need tie handling; the 1/T remark is not an algorithmic cutoff.
correction: Assume a posterior-unique best arm or specify tie-breaking; interpret the threshold as intuition.

title: Adaptivity does not exclude every normal limit
diagnosis: The source categorically denies a normal limit; the earlier translation silently softened it.
correction: The estimators need not be asymptotically normal without suitable design conditions.

title: Use the assignment probability before the current outcome
diagnosis: The probability notation changes between the algorithm and inference pages.
correction: e_tk=P(W_t=k|H_{t-1}); positivity required. Deterministic UCB does not satisfy it for unselected arms.

title: Martingale integrability uses an absolute moment
diagnosis: The source writes E[X_i]<infinity without absolute values.
correction: Require E|X_i|<infinity.

title: Sufficient conditions for the martingale pivot
diagnosis: Constant conditional variance alone does not ensure a CLT or sample variance concentration.
correction: One sufficient regime: IID current rewards, positive predictable e>=c t^-alpha for alpha<1, positive variance, finite fourth moment.

title: Sketch location restored
diagnosis: The first translation described the continuation-page sketches inside page 25 discussion.
correction: Sketches reconstructed with the page 28 count argument.

title: History arguments in the one-step recursion
diagnosis: The scan writes W_2 in V_pi,2(X_1,W_2,X_2) and W_{t+1} at a next-covariate position.
correction: Use V_pi,2(X_1,W_1,X_2) and X_{t+1} in the general next-history argument.

title: Why a surrogate can change the policy target
diagnosis: The blue warning questions the practical surrogate estimator, not the exact weighted-classification algebra.
correction: Exact weighted zero-one classification preserves the objective; an arbitrary surrogate within a restricted class may not. Additional consistency or approximation guarantees are needed.
